workflows.title: Full web assessment
workflows.summary: Map the application, run targeted vulnerability checks, verify impact, and produce evidence-backed findings.
procedure: Map routes, inputs, authentication gates, and exposed assets with api-recon; save a route and role inventory.
Use designated accounts to test API ownership and privilege boundaries; replay each baseline and changed request.
Test only applicable browser and server-side input contexts; capture request, response, and browser or server proof for each result.
Correlate confirmed tests with supplied defender events, then produce findings with exact retest requests.

workflows.title: Reconnaissance and attack surface
workflows.summary: Discover scoped hosts, services, applications, routes, and inputs before selecting test hypotheses.
procedure: Identify the allowed domain and request budget, then run passive DNS, certificate, archive, and public-source discovery.
If BBOT is installed and active probing is permitted, run its selected modules only against the declared scope.
Probe selected discovered hosts and API routes with the available native or installed tools; separate live assets from passive leads.
Save discovered assets, source timestamps, and coverage gaps for follow-up testing.
prerequisites: BBOT CLI for the BBOT step; passive and native discovery can run without it.

workflows.title: API authorization and IDOR
workflows.summary: Build a role/object matrix and test ownership and privilege boundaries with designated accounts.
procedure: Create a matrix of designated users, roles, objects, and expected permissions.
Capture a normal request for each object and action, then replay with one changed identity, object ID, or privilege at a time.
Verify the returned data or committed action against a second owned account; reject status-code-only conclusions.
Record reproducible request pairs and the smallest server-side policy fix.

workflows.title: Cross-site scripting
workflows.summary: Trace reflected, stored, and DOM input contexts and verify browser impact with reproducible evidence.
procedure: Inventory reflected, stored, and DOM sinks, including HTML, attribute, URL, and script contexts.
Select context-specific test strings and send bounded requests through the recorded path.
Verify execution in the browser with an owned test account and capture DOM state and request evidence.
Distinguish encoding, harmless reflection, and actual script execution; document the affected sink.

workflows.title: Command and template injection
workflows.summary: Trace command and template injection paths, test specific hypotheses, and verify execution impact.
procedure: Trace input to command, template, or deserialization sinks and identify reachable prerequisites.
Test one bounded execution hypothesis in the approved environment, retaining the normal response and error path.
Use a harmless unique marker to verify server-side execution; record output or callback evidence and a negative control.
Report the exact source or request path, affected privileges, and remediation.

workflows.title: SQL injection
workflows.summary: Test scoped injection paths, establish database behavior and privileges, and document demonstrated impact.
procedure: Identify parameter and query contexts and capture a normal request for each.
Test syntax and timing or differential behavior with bounded probes; verify against a control input.
Determine only the database privilege and data access necessary to prove impact in the test environment.
Save a replayable request and distinguish confirmed injection from WAF or application errors.

workflows.title: Race conditions and business logic
workflows.summary: Compare concurrent requests and committed state using the native race and request-tampering tools.
procedure: Choose a single-use invariant and read its committed state before testing.
Use race_probe with a bounded burst against disposable test data and record each response.
Read committed state after the burst and repeat once with fresh data to confirm or reject double execution.
Report the broken invariant, request IDs, timing, and transaction or idempotency fix.

workflows.title: HTTP request smuggling
workflows.summary: Check parser disagreements and connection behavior using the source request-smuggling playbook.
procedure: Map the front-end and back-end HTTP versions, connection reuse, and normalization behavior.
Send the source playbook’s low-volume parser-differential probes through an approved isolated path.
Verify any desynchronization with correlated front-end and back-end logs, a normal request, and a negative control.
Stop on unstable connection behavior and document exact framing and remediation.

workflows.title: Server-side request forgery
workflows.summary: Trace server-side fetches and verify reachable trust boundaries using evidence from approved endpoints.
procedure: Identify server-side fetch sinks and expected URL validation behavior.
Use an operator-owned callback or canary endpoint to confirm server-side requests and capture redirects.
Test only explicitly scoped internal or metadata destinations if provided by the operator; separate reachability, file read, and execution claims.
Record the observed trust boundary, blocked paths, and allowlist or egress remediation.

workflows.title: File upload and inclusion
workflows.summary: Assess validation, storage, inclusion paths, and their execution boundaries.
procedure: Map accepted file types, validators, storage paths, retrieval routes, and content-type handling.
Upload inert marker files with one controlled variation at a time and record server-assigned names and responses.
Verify retrieval, inclusion, or execution separately in an isolated environment using harmless markers.
Report the exact boundary crossed and storage, parser, or execution controls that failed.

workflows.title: Deserialization
workflows.summary: Map reachable serialization inputs, frameworks, prerequisites, and reproducible trust-boundary failures.
procedure: Identify reachable serialized inputs and confirm the language, parser, and object types.
Compare normal and malformed inputs to establish that the parser processes attacker-controlled fields.
Run a bounded harmless proof only when a concrete gadget and affected version are established.
Record parser behavior, prerequisites, and a safe format or allowlist remediation.

workflows.title: Prototype pollution
workflows.summary: Trace JavaScript object merge inputs to reachable application behavior and verify the affected path.
procedure: Find object merge or path-assignment inputs in the scoped JavaScript application.
Test a harmless unique property in a disposable object and compare behavior with a clean baseline.
Trace whether the property crosses into a reachable security decision or server-side sink.
Record the affected library or path and a reproducible negative control.

workflows.title: Cache poisoning and deception
workflows.summary: Compare cache keys, shared responses, normalization, and cross-user exposure on the scoped surface.
procedure: Map cache headers, keys, Vary behavior, and user-specific responses.
Compare two designated accounts or harmless marker inputs with cache misses and hits.
Verify whether a shared response reaches the wrong identity using request and cache identifiers.
Document key normalization, poisoning prerequisites, and cache configuration fixes.

workflows.title: Sessions, OAuth, and identity
workflows.summary: Test session boundaries, OAuth/JWT flow assumptions, and designated test-account access.
procedure: Map OAuth redirect, state, nonce, token audience, session renewal, and logout behavior.
Use designated test identities to compare expected account and resource access.
Test one boundary at a time with replayable requests; avoid using third-party or stolen credentials.
Verify actual session or data exposure and preserve both successful and rejected controls.

workflows.title: Cloud and OIDC trust
workflows.summary: Review cloud identity and metadata trust boundaries and verify findings with available account evidence.
procedure: Inventory supplied cloud identity, workload, OIDC, and RBAC configuration.
Check issuer, audience, subject, role assignment, and resource scope with an operator-controlled account.
If a scoped cloud execution context is provided, verify the minimum read-only access needed to prove a hypothesis.
Record exact principal, permission, and trust-policy evidence without printing secret values.

workflows.title: CI/CD security
workflows.summary: Trace repository, workflow, runner, artifact, and token trust boundaries using the supplied pipeline context.
procedure: Map repository events, workflow triggers, runners, artifacts, dependencies, and available token permissions.
Trace untrusted pull-request or artifact data into privileged steps and identify the exact trust boundary.
Use a disposable branch or supplied logs to verify a safe marker path; do not modify production pipeline secrets.
Record the affected workflow revision and a least-privilege or trigger isolation fix.

workflows.title: Origin and WAF assessment
workflows.summary: Compare permitted edge and origin behavior and verify observed filtering and normalization differences.
procedure: Capture a normal request, control identifier, edge response, and origin behavior for the scoped endpoint.
Compare a small authorized set of semantically equivalent encodings, methods, or content types with one variable per request.
Verify application action and defender telemetry; a 200 response alone is not a bypass.
Report the observed policy mismatch and normalizing or origin access control fix.

workflows.title: Attack-chain verification
workflows.summary: Join confirmed findings into impact hypotheses and launch explicit verification work for each link.
procedure: Load confirmed findings and draw each prerequisite, output, affected asset, and trust boundary.
Reject links lacking a demonstrated prerequisite or a shared test identity and scope.
Verify each transition with harmless markers and evidence from the same authorized environment.
Report end-to-end impact only if all links were observed; otherwise save a bounded hypothesis.

workflows.title: Source code assessment
workflows.summary: Follow input-to-sink data flows, test reachable hypotheses, and cite the exact source revision.
procedure: Select the source revision and enumerate entry points, parsers, and privileged sinks.
Trace attacker-controlled data through validation and authorization to a reachable sink.
Create a minimal local regression or harmless proof for each candidate.
Cite exact file and revision and distinguish reachable defects from pattern matches.

workflows.title: Patch and CVE analysis
workflows.summary: Compare fixes and affected paths, verify authoritative advisory evidence, and test the scoped version.
procedure: Identify exact deployed version and obtain a trusted advisory or source patch.
Diff affected and fixed paths, then map changed behavior to reachable application inputs.
Run a bounded regression against the scoped version or supplied fixture.
Record fixed-version evidence, uncertainty, and retest criteria.

workflows.title: Reverse engineering
workflows.summary: Analyze supplied binaries or application packages through the configured REA integration.
procedure: Confirm the REA MCP is connected and the authorized binary is visible on the host-side shared mount.
Open the file, record its hash and provider, then inspect relevant strings, imports, procedures, or graphs.
Save evidence IDs and limitations for each observation; do not treat strings as executed behavior.
Close the binary session and report the exact build and findings.
prerequisites: REA MCP server connected and host-visible shared file path.

workflows.title: AI application assessment
workflows.summary: Test retrieval, instruction, data, and tool trust boundaries in the scoped AI application.
procedure: Map the AI application’s retrieval, prompt, tool, file, and output trust boundaries.
Send controlled test content through one lower-trust surface at a time.
Verify whether the assistant actually crossed a tool or data boundary; compare with an ordinary control.
Report the affected boundary, observed tool trace, and data-handling fix.

workflows.title: Web attack and defense validation
workflows.summary: Run scoped application tests, preserve request evidence, and correlate defender telemetry with the actual test.
procedure: Establish a normal application request and a timestamped defender telemetry baseline.
Run a scoped API authorization or browser-input test with a unique harmless marker and record request IDs.
Verify the application effect and compare the same timestamp, identity, path, and marker in proxy, WAF, app, and SIEM events.
Classify prevention, detection, and gaps from actual events; create a detection or rule change and a repeatable retest.

workflows.title: Endpoint telemetry validation
workflows.summary: Evaluate endpoint control coverage against an explicitly selected simulation and supplied sensor evidence.
procedure: Select an isolated Windows lab host and the exact endpoint behavior to measure.
Capture baseline service, process, and sensor telemetry before a designated lab simulation.
Run the simulation only through an operator-configured Windows lab connector and correlate its time and marker to observed events.
Record blocked, detected, or unobserved outcomes per sensor; report setup gaps when the connector or telemetry is absent.
prerequisites: Isolated Windows lab connector and endpoint sensor telemetry for live simulation.

workflows.title: Detection engineering
workflows.summary: Review the bundled Sigma, Suricata, ATT&CK, and indicator content against provided positive and negative events.
procedure: Select a bundled rule and inventory its required fields and event source.

Run python3 /app/detections/match_events.py --list, then match an operator-supplied JSONL event file with --rule <stem> --events <path> (add --correlation for a correlation rule). Save the JSON result and SHA-256, keeping synthetic fixtures labeled.
Inspect matched clauses, false positives, and unsupported Sigma features rather than assuming every rule was evaluated.
Report rule coverage, fixture results, and exact telemetry requirements.
prerequisites: Operator-supplied JSONL events with the selected rule’s required fields; the image bundles pySigma 2.0.0 and the reference matcher.

workflows.title: Incident investigation
workflows.summary: Build a timeline, test incident hypotheses, and produce evidence-linked investigation and containment recommendations.
procedure: Ingest supplied alerts, host logs, requests, and artifact hashes with their source and time zone.
Build a timestamped timeline and link related identities, hosts, and processes.
Test incident hypotheses against corroborating and contradictory evidence.
Recommend containment and recovery actions separately from actions actually performed.

workflows.title: Evidence and remediation report
workflows.summary: Consolidate existing task evidence, prioritize findings, and produce remediation and retest criteria.
procedure: Collect linked findings, task evidence, affected assets, and source revisions.
Deduplicate overlapping claims and verify each finding’s proof and exposure.
Prioritize by demonstrated impact and affected scope, then write remediation owners and retest steps.
Mark unsupported or incomplete claims clearly and preserve source evidence links.

workflows.title: Host and lateral assessment
workflows.summary: Review the selected host, identity, and management-path evidence using the imported host assessment tools.
procedure: Identify the operator-selected hosts, accounts, management protocols, and approved Windows lab connector.
Inventory reachable management paths and supplied host evidence without inferring credentials from a plan-only tool response.
Validate a designated lab identity and one intended movement path only when a real connector is configured.
Correlate host and network events, then report confirmed access and detection gaps.
prerequisites: Isolated Windows lab connector and designated test identities for live movement.

workflows.title: Operator C2 handoff
workflows.summary: Prepare and track the configured operator-controlled C2 handoff for a scoped task. This records a handoff, not automatic delivery.
procedure: Confirm the C2 handoff flag, local binary path, hash, target scope, and operator-controlled delivery route.
Use c2_stage_implant to record the configured binary metadata and review the intended handoff.
Use c2_deliver_implant only when enabled and record the resulting handoff reference; it does not transmit the binary.
Correlate any separately observed delivery or callback evidence and report unperformed steps as pending.
prerequisites: ARTEX_ENABLE_C2_HANDOFF and a configured local binary for handoff; actual delivery remains separate.
